chunks: Al-Nadr narrated from Muhammad ibn Hashim, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily a group of people who believed in Musa (peace be upon him) said, 'If we were to go to the army of Fir'awn and join it, we would acquire some of his worldly wealth, and then when what we hope for from the arrival of Musa transpires, we will go to him.' So that is what they did. When Musa and those in his company turned to flee, they mounted their mounts and speedily rode towards Musa, hoping to catch up with him and his companions in order to join them. But Allah sent angels who struck the faces of their mounts thereby causing them to return towards the army of Fir'awn. Hence, they were among those who drowned with Fir'awn.
ai.seo_question: What happened to the hypocrites who joined Pharaoh's army with the intention of switching sides?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd* illustrates the concept of *khud'* (self-admiration) and strategic hypocrisy, where a group joined Pharaoh’s camp not out of conviction but for worldly gain, planning to defect to Musa upon his victory. Divine intervention, manifested by angels striking their mounts' faces, physically reversed their course, symbolizing that their inner insincerity dictated their ultimate fate alongside Pharaoh. This serves as a profound Shia scholarly lesson on how superficial adherence without genuine faith leads to being grouped with the disbelievers in the Hereafter.
